name_story.story: Shahrul can be understood through the Arabic form شَهْرُ الْعِزَّة, whose central sense is shahrul; month of honour (malay form). Shahrul is the Malay form of Arabic شَهْرُ الْعِزَّة (Shahr al-ʿIzza), meaning 'month of honour'.

faq.a: Shahrul is associated with the Arabic form شَهْرُ الْعِزَّة, whose core sense is shahrul; month of honour (malay form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Shahrul?
faq.a: Shahrul is associated with Arabic. Shahrul is the Malay form of Arabic شَهْرُ الْعِزَّة (Shahr al-ʿIzza), meaning 'month of honour'.
Yes — the underlying form شَهْرُ الْعِزَّة is Arabic.
Shahrul can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Shahrul should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Shahr al-ʿIzza is a compound of Arabic elements, not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Shahrul mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Shahrul is rendered شہر العزۃ and carries the sense شہر العزۃ، عزت کا مہینہ.

faq.q: What does Shahrul mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Shahrul is rendered شهرالعزه and carries the sense شهرالعزه، ماه عزت.
A romanized syllable approximation is shah-rul. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Shahrul?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Shahrul, shahrul. Script forms are شهر العزه, شهرالعزه, شَهْرُ الْعِزَّة, شہر العزۃ, शहरुल.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
